edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. in Cant. Prologus 5

source_text: Sciendum quoque est quod divina Scriptura refugisse videatur amoris vocabulum et caritatis ac dilectionis frequentius usam. Non tamen omnimodis nomen amoris exclusit. Ubi enim occasionem lapsus non videbat, ibi etiam nomen amoris inseruit. Et nihil interest in Scripturis utrum amor an caritas an dilectio dicatur, dum eadem vis affectus designetur. Paulus quoque: Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi? et rursum: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum. Amor ergo iste de quo in Cantico agitur non carnalis, sed spiritalis est; non cupiditas, sed caritas.
pass_a_gloss: To-be-known also is that divine Scripture to-have-avoided seems of-love the-word and of-charity and of-dilectio more-often to-have-used. Not however altogether name of-amor it-excluded... And nothing it-matters in Scriptures whether amor or caritas or dilectio is-said, while same force of-affection is-designated...
pass_b_english: It should also be known that divine Scripture seems to have avoided the word amor and to have used caritas and dilectio more often. Yet it has not altogether shut out the name amor. For where it did not see occasion of falling, there it also inserted the name amor. And it makes no difference in the Scriptures whether amor or caritas or dilectio is said, so long as the same force of affection is designated. Paul too: Who will separate us from the charity of Christ? and again: You shall love the Lord your God. This love, therefore, of which the Song treats is not carnal but spiritual; not cupidity, but charity.
